title: GPU utilization synchrony matrix - weekly export
content:
Summary:
This sheet is a weekly sampling export focused on GPU cross-pool synchrony and short-tail vs. long-tail utilization patterns across clusters. The goal is to detect periods where multiple pools (reserved, burst, spot) simultaneously hit high utilization ("synchrony"), which reduces effective headroom and increases risk of cross-tenant interference during surge windows.

What this export contains (columns):
- sample_date: UTC date for the sampling window (daily snapshot at 00:00 UTC)
- cluster: cluster short name (e.g., na-west-1a-01)
- pool: pool id / logical name (reserved / burst / spot / training)
- avg_util_pct: 24h average GPU utilization (0-100)
- p95_util_pct: 95th percentile of per-GPU utilization over 24h
- p99_util_pct: 99th percentile (captures microbursts)
- tail_latency_ms: 95th percentile request tail latency in ms (for hosted inference routes)
- thermal_headroom_pct: estimated percentage of thermal headroom remaining (based on recent telemetry and power capping heuristics)
- co_schedule_index: synchrony metric (0-1) — fraction of top-10 utilization minutes that overlap across >1 pool on the same cluster
- tilt_index: short-term drift metric (difference between weekly avg and last 6-hour rolling avg, signed)
- incidents: count of capacity-related fallbacks or throttles recorded in the window
- notes: free-text ops notes and quick pointers

Sample rows (truncated):
sample_date,cluster,pool,avg_util_pct,p95_util_pct,p99_util_pct,tail_latency_ms,thermal_headroom_pct,co_schedule_index,tilt_index,incidents,notes
2026-12-08,na-west-1a-01,reserved,62,88,96,18,28,0.67,5,2,"Evening surge from two tenants; manual burst enabled 21:10-21:45 UTC"
2026-12-08,na-west-1a-01,burst,48,76,92,22,44,0.67,3,1,"Burst pool consumed spot capacity during microburst; consider stricter preemption window"
2026-12-08,eu-central-2b-03,spot,31,59,83,45,62,0.22,-2,0,"Low spot pressure; p99 spikes align with nightly training job ramp at 02:00 UTC"
2026-12-08,apac-south-1c-02,training,71,93,98,120,12,0.82,9,3,"Training job packing inefficiency; thermal headroom low, VM-level power capping engaged"

Methodology notes (how synchrony/co_schedule_index is computed):
- For each cluster we derive the top-10 minutes by aggregate GPU utilization over a 24h window. co_schedule_index = (# of those minutes where more than one pool's per-GPU utilization > 75%) / 10. This highlights short high-concurrency pressure events not visible in daily averages.
- tilt_index = (avg_util_last_7d - avg_util_last_6h). Positive => recent increase. Values reported in percentage points.
- thermal_headroom_pct uses a heuristic combining GPU temp, reported power budget, and recent throttle events; accuracy ~±6%.

Key observations this week:
- NA clusters: elevated synchrony in reserved+burst pools on two clusters (na-west-1a-01 and na-east-2c-05). co_schedule_index > 0.6 indicates overlapping microbursts from several tenants. Result: two fallbacks to model-variant with higher latency recorded (JIRA-OPS-4872).
- APAC training cluster apac-south-1c-02 shows sustained high avg utilization and p99 ~98%. Thermal headroom low => risk of longer cooling-induced throttles. Training packing and node-level power capping seem to be interacting badly — see notes and linked PR.
- EU region currently has low spot pressure; good opportunity to rebalance non-latency workloads into eu-central clusters overnight.

Quick quantitative recommendations:
1) Short-term (0-48h): add preemption windows for burst pool on na-west-1a-01 between 20:00-02:00 UTC to reduce co-scheduling overlap. (Owner: Benji)
2) Medium-term (3-14d): enable bin-packing optimization for training workloads in APAC that enforces thermal-headroom-aware scheduling. Target reduction of tilt_index by 6–8 percentage points. (Owner: David)
3) Operational rule: alert when co_schedule_index > 0.6 AND thermal_headroom_pct < 20% for any cluster — create an automated runway action to increase burst headroom.

Action items and follow-ups:
- Benji: implement and test preemption window; update load-shedding config. Link: JIRA-OPS-4875.
- David: validate training job placement heuristics with infra-sim; propose config changes by 2026-12-12.
- Lena: add co_schedule_index to daily ops dashboard and set a soft alert at 0.45.
- Marta: coordinate with SRE on automatic thermal headroom sampling to improve heuristic accuracy (create perf test).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we lower the p99 guardrail for hosted inference in clusters with co_schedule_index > 0.5? Pros: avoids repeated fallbacks; Cons: increases cost from stricter headroom.
- Can we get per-tenant correlation metrics (which tenant groups drive the overlap) without leaking PII? Need a short privacy-safe aggregation design (see CONFLUENCE-1223).

Raw download notes:
- This export was generated from the weekly-telemetry pipeline (export job id: telemetry-export-2026-12-08-03). Sampling is deterministic for reproducibility.
- Columns align with the capacity planning sheet schema v2.1 (see linked Confluence page).

Ops shorthand & quick links:
- dashboard: /dashboards/gpu-sync-matrix-weekly
- runbook: /playbooks/gpu-thermal-and-surge
- short ticket: JIRA-OPS-4872 (fallback incidents)

If anything looks off in the numbers, ping me on #infra-gpu with the row and sample_date; I'll trace back to raw telemetry.
